box.english: Could you review the report, please?

last_email.angle: Gratitude: thank one person for something specific and concrete they did this week.

today.body:
After I finish my lunch break, I will send a one‑sentence text to the new person I met this week saying something like, “Hi, I enjoyed our chat.”
Floor version: type the sentence and hit send in under 30 seconds.
Reason: a brief, concrete outreach turns a pleasant encounter into a real connection (strong).
Español del día: ¿Cómo está la línea? (Say it just after you log in, before starting your checks).

Note from M: I kept it to one tiny step today. Let me know if it feels too small or too big.

Confirmed by M: I received 1 email from you.
- Your email "✅ Buy-day check: $75 today": read by the Mentor and noted.

b.advice: Tie the greeting to the exact moment you unlock your computer (cue) and then walk straight to the nearest inspection station (stack). Use a concrete if‑then: If I log in at 8:00 am, then I will say “Buenos días, ¿cómo va la línea hoy?” and follow with one specific question about the line. Keep the fallback version (“Buenos días”) ready for a rough day. Count the success on a simple tally sheet right after the conversation – a single check mark is the reward and proof the habit occurred.

t.lesson: After you log into your computer at 8:00 am, walk to the nearest inspection station and say: “¿Cómo está la línea?” Then note a check‑mark on a sheet to record completion.
